title: The Quiet Garden
premise: Petra Dravenmoor, a lighthouse keeper's grandson and part-time novelist, has spent five years rebuilding a quiet life around his late grandmother's struggling bakery, measured in small safe steps after a public scandal destroyed his first career. When a local literary society's anonymous pen-pal assignment pairs him with Vivian Ashcroft—the sharp-tongued developer whose company holds the bakery's lease and whom he publicly humiliated years ago—neither realizes at first who is on the other end of the letters. As their written intimacy deepens while their daytime rivalry over the lease turns bitter, Petra must choose between the anonymity that saved him and the truth that could save them both. In the end, he reveals himself in a letter read aloud at the society's gala, forfeiting the anonymous prize money that would have covered the lease, and Vivian—having already discovered and fallen for the man behind the pen—chooses to renegotiate the bakery into a partnership rather than a demolition.
about_author: Sable Oyelaran is a former coastal archivist who writes slow-burn romances about people who rebuild themselves from wreckage. They live above a bookshop with an opinionated cat and a growing collection of unsent letters.

chapters.title: The Lighthouse Keeps Nothing
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Five years after fleeing a scandal in the city, Petra measures his days in flour, tide charts, and chapters of an unpublished novel, tending his grandmother's bakery below the old lighthouse. When the landlord's notice arrives—a lease review by Ashcroft Development—his careful calm cracks. Emotional beat: the fragile peace of a life built on avoidance.

chapters.title: Assigned Correspondents
chapters.summary: Vivian's POV. The Saltmere Literary Society launches its annual anonymous pen-pal winter exchange; Vivian joins on a whim between site inspections, half-hoping to understand the town she's contracted to redevelop. She draws a correspondent called 'Keeper' whose dry wit unsettles her. Emotional beat: curiosity disguised as obligation.

chapters.title: Letters Against Demolition
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. By day, Petra confronts Vivian at a hostile community meeting about the bakery block; by night, 'Keeper' and 'Wren' trade confessions neither would say aloud. Each begins suspecting the other of hiding something. Emotional beat: the delicious irony of intimacy built on enemy ground.

chapters.title: What Grandmother Left
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Sorting his grandmother's papers, Petra finds her original deed—and a clause giving the Ashcroft family right of first refusal, explaining Vivian's personal stake in the property. He also finds her unsent letters to a lost love, mirroring his own. Emotional beat: inheritance as burden, not gift.

chapters.title: The Face Across the Table
chapters.summary: Vivian's POV. A storm strands Vivian in the bakery overnight; Petra's kindness contradicts everything her board expects of the town. Rereading Wren's latest letter that night, a phrase strikes her—she suspects Keeper is Petra. Emotional beat: recognition as vertigo.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Vivian offers a deal: sign away the building quietly and she'll fund his novel's publication—an escape back to the career he abandoned. Tempted, he nearly accepts, then writes Wren the most honest letter yet without signing his name. Emotional beat: loyalty to a dead woman's dream versus hunger for redemption.

chapters.title: Boardroom Ghosts
chapters.summary: Vivian's POV. Her firm demands the demolition timeline accelerate; her mentor reveals the Ashcroft family history with the Dravenmoors—her grandfather was the lost love in grandmother's letters. Vivian realizes the lease fight is an inherited wound, not business. Emotional beat: the past demanding payment.

chapters.title: The Unsent Letter
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra discovers Vivian knows—or will soon—and preempts exposure by withdrawing from the pen-pal program, leaving Wren a final unsigned letter confessing everything except his name. Vivian receives it and recognizes his handwriting from the lease documents. Emotional beat: cowardice that is somehow braver than honesty.

chapters.title: Gala, Glasshouse, Gala
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. At the society's winter gala, the reveal ceremony unmasks all correspondents. Before Vivian can speak, Petra takes the stage, reads his own confession aloud, and publicly declines the prize money that might have saved the bakery—choosing truth over rescue. Emotional beat: climax; identity claimed at maximum cost.

chapters.title: First Refusal
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, closing with a shared scene. Vivian renegotiates: the bakery becomes a joint preservation project under grandmother's deed clause, and her resignation letter sits unsent beside his finished manuscript. On the lighthouse gallery, they exchange real names like vows. Emotional beat: resolution—truth and loyalty reconciled, inheritance reclaimed together.
